summary: Tested the web preview fix, login and logout UI, the password change (API + UI, including logging out the other device with 2 browser contexts), dish labels (allergens, preset and custom tags), tenant isolation regression (32/32), landing page and images, and the deploy files (static review only). Everything requested works. One minor backend gap: after a password change, the old access token is still accepted on /api/auth/* routes (/me, /change-password) until it expires. Pizzeria Napoli password restored to Password123! and checked (login returns 200). Giorgio Bistrot was not touched.

minor.issue: After a password change, the other device's old access token still returns 200 on /api/auth/me (and can call /api/auth/change-password if it knows the new password). TenantContextMiddleware skips the password_version (pv) check for the /api/auth prefix, and get_current_user does not check pv either. Data routes correctly return 401, so the UI still logs out the other device.

issues: The 'Nuovo' and 'Categorie' buttons, the dish name/price inputs and the search input have no testID (tests had to use text/placeholder selectors)

action_items: Optional hardening: make get_current_user (or the change-password and /me routes) check claim pv against users.password_version, so an old token is rejected on /api/auth/* too
Add testIDs to the Dishes screen controls: Nuovo, Categorie, search, name and price inputs
critical_code_review_comments: tenancy.py: the pv cache is per process (30 s), and invalidate_password_version only clears the local process. With several uvicorn workers or Railway replicas, other workers keep accepting old tokens for up to 30 s. Fine with the current single-worker Dockerfile.railway; document this or check pv in the DB if workers are added.
The register endpoint does not set the pv claim. It works because the default is 0, but for consistency add extra_claims pv=0 and legacy=False.

server.py: CORS has allow_credentials=True with the default origin '*'. The app uses Bearer tokens, so there is no cookie risk, but in production set CORS_ORIGINS to the Vercel domain (the docs already say so).
The test suite needs EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL exported: test_tenant_isolation.py crashes at collection when it is not set (it reads os.environ with no fallback).
Playbook check: the app uses Bearer tokens stored on the client, not httpOnly cookies (by design for tablets). Brute-force lockout is present (5 fails -> 15 min).

success_rate.backend: 98% (43/44; the 1 failure is the minor stale-token-on-/auth/me finding)

seed_data_creation: Pizzeria Napoli only: dishes 'TEST_Pizza Labels' (6aeca2921b19d4b28b4c033e) and 'TEST_UI Dish' (6aeca2aa1b19d4b28b4c0340), both deactivated afterwards (the API only soft-deletes). The test runs created and revoked refresh tokens. The leftover TEST_Cat_* categories in Pizzeria Napoli come from earlier runs.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run the tests one at a time with EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL exported: python -m pytest tests/test_change_password.py -p no:xdist. test_change_password.py restores the password in a module teardown. The UI passed: preview root redirects to /login, wrong-password error, login and reload persistence, Report header controls, modal validations, 2-context logout of the other device (B ends on the login screen after a tab switch, A stays logged in after reload), password restored via the modal, double-tap logout, dish labels saved and shown. Wrong logins used: 1 in UI, about 3 in pytest (each success resets the counter).
rca of the issue: Blank preview: fixed. +html.tsx now renders headNodes and bodyNodes from useServerDocumentContext; the app JS loads and redirects to /login.
